lyrics:
[Intro: tambourine, bass and drums driving, a horn stab]

[Verse 1: male tenor, warm and quick]
Now if you ever need me, I don't care about the hour
I don't care about the weather or the miles
You've got my number written on the wall beside the phone
One ring and I'm reaching for the keys

[Chorus: both voices, horns and tambourine]
Say the word and I'm driving
Through the dark and the rain
Pick a town, name a time
I've already left the lane
Say the word

[Verse 2: female soprano, bright and sure]
When we said goodbye at the station gate
I made you a promise I don't break
You call, I come, it's a simple thing
You don't even have to let it ring

[Chorus: both voices, horns and tambourine]
Say the word and I'm driving
Through the dark and the rain
Pick a town, name a time
I've already left the lane
Say the word

[Bridge: voices trading short lines, drums pushing]
(If the bridge is out) I'll find a boat
(If the road is closed) I'll walk
(If you can't speak) I'll hear you anyway
Just knock

[Final Chorus: both voices ad-libbing, strings on top]
Say the word and I'm driving
Through the dark and the rain
Pick a town, name a time
I've already left the lane
Say the word
Oh, say the word

[Outro: band vamps, voices trading "say it", fade]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 130 BPM, 4/4, D major. A bright, driving Motown beat that never lets up. Joyful and sure.

VOICE: A man with a smooth, sweet, agile tenor and a woman with a bright, clear soprano. They take a verse each, sing the chorus together, and trade short lines in the bridge, each finishing the other's thought. Ad-libs over the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A melodic, busy electric bass. A snare on every beat with a tambourine. A baritone saxophone doubling the bass line. A horn section. Piano and vibraphone. Chiming rhythm guitar on the backbeat. A string section in the last chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, tambourine, bass and a horn stab. 0:08 Verse 1, the man. 0:30 Chorus 1. 0:48 Verse 2, the woman. 1:10 Chorus 2. 1:28 Bridge, traded lines. 1:46 Final chorus with strings and ad-libs. 2:10 Outro, the band vamps as the voices trade two words, fading by 2:30.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1960s Detroit soul: punchy, bright and dense, bass and tambourine loud, voices on top, a little natural echo.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first chorus, when the second voice joins at 0:30.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The mountain and the river become a car, a number on the wall and a long road at night. It is the promise families make across distance, said by people old enough to have kept it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Assurance, answered assurance, joy.
